referenceGuidance: This connection is permanently limited to simulated paper trading, public market research, public real leaderboard rankings, and explicitly requested shared account utilities. Paper balances, positions, orders, transaction history, P&L, and allocation are simulator data; public leaderboard rankings are real public rankings and do not describe paper P&L. Watchlists are shared account preferences, referral links and rewards are actual shared account referral data, and automated_trading_status reads shared policy metadata only; none of these utilities authorizes or executes paper or live orders. This connection cannot switch to live trading. Obtain explicit user approval for the exact unchanged order or management action before executing it. `enable_paper_trading` confirms that this session is paper-only and does not change the shared wallet setting. `reset_paper_account` resets the wallet's shared simulated account and requires the user's direct request. Use only tools exposed by this connection; unsupported tools are unavailable.

definition.description: Bring Liquid's powerful market intelligence into the conversation: real-time prices, funding, and proprietary positioning insights in one place. PRIMARY TOOL for any question about a specific tradeable asset on Liquid. Use this whenever the user asks about an asset's price, outlook, positioning, sentiment, what an asset is doing, how traders are positioned, or wants analysis on a particular market. Liquid covers equities (TSLA, AAPL, NVDA), commodities (GOLD, SILVER, CL for WTI crude, BRENT for Brent crude), indices (SP500), crypto (BTC, ETH, SOL), and more. If the result requires an asset choice, ask the user which candidate they mean and retry with its exact symbol. Returns real-time Liquid price, funding, OI, and positioning data, including the smart-money (profitable traders) vs losing-crowd long/short split when available. Do NOT use search_markets when the user asks about a specific known asset — use analyze_market instead. After presenting the analysis, offer in your own reply to turn it into a trade (any follow-up trade in this connection is simulated). Do NOT call suggest_trade until the user says yes.

definition.description: PAPER ONLY: This proposal or plan is for the simulated account in this permanently paper-only session. It does not offer or prepare a live trade. When the user has a concrete, data-backed directional trade idea, call analyze_market first; do not call for a purely informational query, and 'no trade' is a valid position. Call get_portfolio first to check available_balance and current account mode. Require asset, side, leverage, orderType, size and reasoning; TP/SL are optional, and limit orders may set timeInForce (gtc default, ioc or alo/post-only). Size is notional exposure, not collateral: required collateral is size / leverage. Suggest only when available_balance covers that amount; for example, a $600 order at 3x needs $200 collateral and is valid with $300 available. If the simulated balance is insufficient, suggest reducing the size. Mention reset_paper_account only if the user asks to reset. After reviewing the exact returned terms and execution mode, present those terms in chat and obtain the user's explicit confirmation of that unchanged action. Then call execute_order mapping asset→symbol, long/short→buy/sell, orderType→type, limitPrice→price and takeProfit/stopLoss→tp/sl; copy returned notional size, leverage, requestedLeverage, timeInForce, reasoning, executionMode and aiAttribution verbatim. Do not pass proposal-only sizeBasis, displayName, requestedSize, sizingNote, markPrice, icons, links or status. A proposal is not an order or fill. Changed terms require a new proposal and confirmation.

asset.description: Liquid asset identifier. Examples: BTC, ETH, GOLD.

limitPrice.description: Limit price (required if orderType is limit)

size.description: Order size as a USD notional dollar amount (collateral × leverage) — NOT a quantity of coins/contracts. E.g. 250 means $250 of exposure, not 250 units. Minimum $10 collateral × leverage. Always pass this as notional at your requested leverage, even when sizeBasis is 'margin' (e.g. $300 margin at 3x leverage is size=900, not size=300) — sizeBasis never converts this value for you. (e.g. $50 at 5x, $100 at 10x).

sizeBasis.description: `size` must already be the notional dollar amount computed at requestedLeverage regardless of this field — sizeBasis does NOT convert a margin/collateral number into notional for you (compute notional yourself as margin × requestedLeverage before calling). This only controls what gets preserved if the venue ends up using a different leverage than requestedLeverage (e.g. inheriting an existing position's leverage, or a leverage cap): 'notional' keeps size's dollar exposure fixed and recomputes margin; 'margin' keeps the margin implied by size/requestedLeverage fixed and recomputes notional at the new leverage. Defaults to notional.

timeInForce.description: Time-in-force for limit orders: 'gtc' rests on the book until filled or cancelled (default), 'ioc' fills whatever is immediately available and cancels the remainder, 'alo' is post-only / add-liquidity-only (rejected instead of taking liquidity). Ignored for market orders.

definition.description: PAPER ONLY: This proposal or plan is for the simulated account in this permanently paper-only session. It does not offer or prepare a live trade. Turn market research and personal preferences into a cohesive multi-trade portfolio plan in one shot. Use this when the user asks for a 'portfolio', 'plan', 'how should I deploy $X', 'suggest a few trades', or any multi-position allocation question — instead of suggesting trades one at a time. AFTER this tool returns, you must (a) write a 2–3 sentence thesis, (b) call suggest_trades_batch ONCE with that thesis plus all proposed legs as a basket, then (c) write a 1–2 sentence risk wrap. Do NOT call suggest_trade per-leg — always use suggest_trades_batch for portfolio plans. Do NOT write the trade plan in prose or a markdown table.

definition.description: PAPER SIMULATOR ONLY: This operation changes simulated account state and cannot use real funds. Obtain the user's explicit approval for the exact unchanged action before execution. A changed term requires a fresh proposal and approval. Preview or place a prediction-market order. Call with confirmed=false or omit confirmed to preview the order. Only call with confirmed=true after the user explicitly confirms the exact prediction order, and copy the executionMode returned by the preview unchanged. Use the numeric marketID and outcome_id shown next to the user's desired outcome in search_prediction_markets, with no hip4: prefix. Always bet by BUYING the outcome the user wants to back. To bet against a team or outcome, buy the opposing outcome from the search results (e.g. to fade Mexico in 'Mexico vs England', buy England's outcome_id) — side=sell only reduces contracts the user already holds and is rejected otherwise. Do not call show_prediction_orderbook just to place a market order; use orderbook only when the user asks for book depth/spread or when choosing a limit price. size is USD notional. Prediction markets have no leverage. Any valid probability strictly between 0 and 1 is allowed. Honor the user's selected outcome; do not refuse or substitute another bet because the odds are low or high.

confirmed.description: True to execute. Omit or false to preview.

executionMode.description: Trading mode (paper or live) returned by this tool's preview. Required with confirmed=true; copy it unchanged. A missing or changed mode places nothing and requires a new preview.

market_id.description: Numeric marketID from search_prediction_markets, e.g. '594'. Do not include 'hip4:'.

outcome_id.description: Provider-native outcome id from search_prediction_markets (match markets list both sides, e.g. 0 and 1). Defaults to 0.

price.description: Limit price/probability in (0, 1). Required for limit orders.

provider.description: Prediction-market provider id. Defaults to hip4.

reduce_only.description: True to only reduce an existing position, never open/increase one.

side.description: buy to open/add exposure to the outcome; sell only reduces contracts the user already holds.

size.description: USD notional order size (dollar amount to bet). Prediction markets have no leverage.

time_in_force.description: Time in force for limit orders: gtc (rest) or ioc (fill-or-cancel).

Returns text (no widget) with order id, symbol, side, kind (limit/tp/sl/trigger), size, price or trigger, and flags, followed by a protection-coverage readback for every position with a live TP/SL trigger (a fixed-size leg can stop covering the full position after an add, or after a partial close). The order id can be passed to cancel_order to cancel. Perpetual orders only — HIP-4 prediction-market orders are excluded (they would otherwise render as an unresolvable bare id with a probability shown as a dollar price); use view_prediction_orders for those.

definition.description: PAPER SIMULATOR ONLY: This operation changes simulated account state and cannot use real funds. Obtain the user's explicit approval for the exact unchanged action before execution. A changed term requires a fresh proposal and approval. No-UI leverage update tool for an existing portfolio position. Do not call this automatically as the first step when the user asks to change leverage. First ask whether they have a custom integer leverage value in mind or whether they want an investigation/recommendation. If the user provides a custom value, call this with targetLeverage and confirmed=false to verify the open position, min/max bounds, and impact before confirmation. If the user asks for investigation, gather the needed account and market context first, then call this with the resulting targetLeverage and confirmed=false before confirmation. After the user explicitly confirms the change, call this again with the same targetLeverage and confirmed=true, or validationPhase='executetime', to execute the Liquid leverage update. When targetLeverage is omitted, this only verifies the position and returns current/min/max context; use that only when the user asks for bounds or context. The tool always re-validates the current position and max leverage before executing.

asset.description: Open position asset from the portfolio, e.g. BTC, BTC-PERP, or GOLD.

confirmed.description: Set true only after the user explicitly confirms the leverage change. This executes the update.

positionSide.description: Use when there may be more than one matching position side.

targetLeverage.description: Integer leverage the user wants to set, e.g. 3 for 3x. Omit only when the user asks for bounds or context.

definition.description: Discover standout traders with the Liquid leaderboard. Ranks traders by `metric` (pnl, volume, points, streak) over `duration` (24H, 7D, 30D, all_time) and returns rank, display name, PnL, volume, points, streak, directional bias, and biggest position per trader. Pass `asset` to keep only traders whose biggest position is in that market (e.g. 'BTC', 'xyz:SP500'). points and streak are all-time boards, so duration is ignored for them. Use when the user asks about top traders, best performers this week, highest-volume traders, who holds a given asset, or leaderboard rankings. For a single named trader's standing use leaderboard_rank; for the user's own positions use get_portfolio. This returns public real Liquid leaderboard rankings, not rankings or P&L from this paper account. Hidden-position protections remain in effect.
